```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_scip <- requireNamespace("scip", quietly = TRUE)
has_osqp <- requireNamespace("osqp", quietly = TRUE)
has_nloptr <- requireNamespace("nloptr", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(optcompR)
```

optcompR describes an optimization problem once, as variables, expressions,
constraints and an objective, and then classifies it, chooses a capable solver
Integer and binary variables turn an LP into a MILP (or a QP into a MIQP).
Branch and bound solvers report an incumbent objective, a proven bound and the
relative gap between them.

## Knapsack

```{r}
value <- c(10, 13, 7, 8, 12, 4)
weight <- c(5, 7, 3, 4, 6, 2)
m <- opt_model("max")
take <- opt_variable(m, "take", dim = 6, type = "binary")
cap <- opt_constraint(m, sum(weight * take) <= 15, name = "capacity")
opt_objective(m, sum(value * take))
r <- opt_solve(m)
opt_status(r)
which(opt_value(r, take) > 0.5)
c(objective = opt_objective_value(r), bound = opt_objective_bound(r),
  gap = opt_gap(r))
```

## Facility location with fixed costs

Binary open decisions link to continuous flows through big M constraints.

```{r}
fixed <- c(30, 25, 40)
unit <- matrix(c(2, 4, 5,
                 3, 1, 3,
                 4, 3, 1,
                 5, 4, 2), 4, byrow = TRUE)  # 4 customers by 3 sites
demand <- c(10, 15, 12, 8)
m2 <- opt_model()
open <- opt_variable(m2, "open", dim = 3, type = "binary")
flow <- opt_variable(m2, "flow", dim = c(4, 3), lower = 0)
for (i in 1:4) opt_constraint(m2, sum(flow[i, ]) == demand[i])
for (j in 1:3) opt_constraint(m2, sum(flow[, j]) <= sum(demand) * open[j])
opt_objective(m2, sum(fixed * open) + sum(unit * flow))
r2 <- opt_solve(m2)
opt_value(r2, open)
opt_objective_value(r2)
```

## Limits and gaps

```{r}
r3 <- opt_solve(m2, mip_gap = 0.05, time_limit = 10)
opt_status(r3)
opt_gap(r3)
```

A `time_limit` status with a feasible point is a usable but unproven
solution: `opt_has_solution()` tells whether a point exists, and the gap tells
how far it may be from optimal.

## Duals of a MILP

Integer programs have no duals in the LP sense. `opt_fixed_relaxation()`
fixes the integer variables at their optimal values and solves the remaining
LP, whose duals are the usual marginal values for that fixed configuration.

```{r}
fr <- opt_fixed_relaxation(r)
opt_dual(fr, cap)
```

## Mixed-integer quadratic problems

```{r, eval = has_scip}
m4 <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m4, "x", dim = 3, type = "integer", lower = -5, upper = 5)
opt_objective(m4, sum((x - c(1.4, -2.6, 0.5))^2))
r4 <- opt_solve(m4)
r4$solver
opt_value(r4, x)
```
